2.w: “Truly, I know that this is so. But how can a human be just before God?

3.w: If someone wishes to contend with him, he cannot answer him one time in a thousand.

4.w: He is wise in heart and mighty in strength — who has resisted him and remained safe?

5.w: He who removes mountains suddenly, who overturns them in his anger,

6.w: he who shakes the earth out of its place so that its pillars tremble,

7.w: he who commands the sun, and it does not shine and seals up the stars,

8.w: he alone spreads out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.

9.w: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the constellations of the southern sky;

10.w: he does great and unsearchable things, and wonderful things without number.

11.w: If he passes by me, I cannot see him; if he goes by, I cannot perceive him.

12.w: If he snatches away, who can turn him back? Who dares to say to him, ‘What are you doing?’

13.w: God does not restrain his anger; under him the helpers of Rahab lie crushed.

14.w: “How much less, then, can I answer him and choose my words to argue with him.

15.w: Although I am innocent, I could not answer him; I could only plead with my judge for mercy.

16.w: If I summoned him and he answered me, I would not believe that he would be listening to my voice—

17.w: he who crushes me with a tempest and multiplies my wounds for no reason.

18.w: He does not allow me to recover my breath, for he fills me with bitterness.

19.w: If it is a matter of strength, most certainly he is the strong one! And if it is a matter of justice, he will say, ‘Who will summon me?’

20.w: Although I am innocent, my mouth would condemn me; although I am blameless, it would declare me perverse.

21.w: I am blameless. I do not know myself. I despise my life.

22.w: “It is all one! That is why I say, ‘He destroys the blameless and the guilty.’

23.w: If a scourge brings sudden death, he mocks at the despair of the innocent.

24.w: If a land has been given into the hand of a wicked man, he covers the faces of its judges; if it is not he, then who is it?

25.w: “My days are swifter than a runner, they speed by without seeing happiness.

26.w: They glide by like reed boats, like an eagle that swoops down on its prey.

27.w: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will change my expression and be cheerful,’

28.w: I dread all my sufferings, for I know that you do not hold me blameless.

29.w: If I am guilty, why then weary myself in vain?

30.w: If I wash myself with snow-melt water and make my hands clean with lye,

31.w: then you plunge me into a slimy pit and my own clothes abhor me.

32.w: For he is not a human being like I am, that I might answer him, that we might come together in judgment.

33.w: Nor is there an arbiter between us, who might lay his hand on us both,

34.w: who would take his rod away from me so that his terror would not make me afraid.

35.w: Then would I speak and not fear him, but it is not so with me.
